:::{#def-surprisal}
#### Surprisal (**self-information**, **information content**)

The **surprisal** of a possible value $x$ of a [discrete random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-discrete-rv) $X$
with $\P(X=x) > 0$ is

$$\surprisalf{x} \eqdef -\log \P(X=x).$$

The surprisal is also called the **self-information** [@goodfellow2016deep, p. 73]
or the **information content** [@bishop2006prml, p. 49] of $x$.
With the natural logarithm, the surprisal is measured in nats, and with base 2 in bits.
Evaluating $\surprisalf{\cdot}$ at the [random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable) $X$ itself gives the random variable $\surprisalf{X}$, which equals $\surprisalf{x}$ when $X = x$.
The notation leaves the [probability mass function](random-variables.qmd#def-pmf) of $X$ implicit.

:::
